text: Quick SEO check you can do in 10 seconds: open your homepage, view source, search for <title>. If it's missing, empty, or the same on every page, that's the first thing to fix.
Many sites block AI crawlers without knowing it. A single "Disallow: /" under "User-agent: *" in robots.txt also stops GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot. Worth checking once.
Meta descriptions don't directly affect rankings, but they often become the snippet people read before clicking. Aim for roughly 120-160 characters and write it for humans.
One H1 per page is a good habit. It tells both readers and crawlers what the page is about. Multiple H1s aren't fatal, but they usually mean the structure is unclear.
Broken internal links waste crawl budget and frustrate visitors. Even a small site can pick up dozens of 404s after a redesign or a URL change. Audit after every big update.

Is your site ready for AI search? Check robots.txt for AI crawlers, add a clear title and description to every page, and consider an llms.txt file. This tool checks all of it in one run:
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/seo-ai-readiness-audit
Canonical tags tell search engines which URL is the "real" one when the same content lives at several addresses (http/https, with/without www, URL parameters). Missing canonicals = diluted signals.
llms.txt is a simple Markdown file at your site root that summarizes your important pages for AI models. It's still a proposal, but it's cheap to add and easy to keep updated.
Images without alt text are invisible to screen readers and give search engines less context. Describe what the image shows in a short, plain sentence.

A page set to noindex by accident can stay hidden from Google for months. Check both the meta robots tag and the X-Robots-Tag HTTP header. This audit flags both on every page:
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/seo-ai-readiness-audit
Thin pages (very little text, no clear purpose) rarely rank and rarely get cited by AI answers. Merge them, expand them, or noindex them.
Structured data (JSON-LD) helps search engines understand what a page is: an article, a product, an FAQ, an organization. It's also a strong signal for AI-generated answers.

Run a full-site SEO + AI search readiness audit: per-page issues, an SEO score, an AI readiness score, AI crawler access, broken links and a ready-to-use llms.txt. No setup:
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/seo-ai-readiness-audit
The <html lang> attribute is easy to forget. It helps browsers, screen readers and search engines serve your page to the right audience. One attribute, zero cost.
Missing Open Graph tags mean ugly link previews on social apps: no image, random text. og:title and og:image take two minutes to add and make every share look better.

Missing a mobile viewport meta tag? Your page may render as a tiny desktop layout on phones. Google uses mobile-first indexing, so this matters for rankings too. Check yours here:
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/seo-ai-readiness-audit
GEO (generative engine optimization) is mostly good SEO done well: clear headings, direct answers, accurate facts, and pages that AI crawlers are allowed to read.
Before blocking AI crawlers, decide what you want. Blocking GPTBot stops training crawls, while OAI-SearchBot is used for ChatGPT search results. They are different bots.

Agencies: an AI search readiness score is an easy add-on to a normal SEO audit, and clients increasingly ask why ChatGPT never mentions them. This Actor exports an HTML report in English or Japanese:
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/seo-ai-readiness-audit
Duplicate titles across many pages make it hard for search engines to tell them apart. Give each page a title that says what's unique about it.
A quick win for AI answers: put a one or two sentence direct answer near the top of the page, then the details below. Both readers and AI models appreciate it.

Want an llms.txt but don't want to write it by hand? This Actor crawls your site and generates one from your own pages, along with a full SEO and AI readiness report:
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/seo-ai-readiness-audit
Redirect chains (A -> B -> C) slow down crawlers and users. Point old URLs straight to the final destination with a single 301.
Don't rely on one audit. Sites change: new pages, new plugins, a robots.txt edit by someone on the team. A monthly check catches problems before traffic drops.

Checklist for any new page: unique title, meta description, one H1, canonical, alt text on images, internal links in and out, indexable. Or check a whole site at once:
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/seo-ai-readiness-audit
External links that now return 404 hurt user trust more than rankings, but they're still worth fixing. Replace them or remove them during your regular content review.
Tip: compare your AI crawler rules with a competitor's robots.txt. You can learn a lot about how other sites approach AI search just by reading that one file.

Good SEO in one sentence: make every page easy to find, easy to understand, and genuinely useful. Everything else is details.

Core Web Vitals in one line each: LCP = how fast the main content shows (aim under 2.5s). CLS = how much the layout jumps (under 0.1). INP/TBT = how quickly the page reacts to taps.
The fastest page-speed win on most sites: compress and resize hero images. A 3 MB photo shown at 800px wide is the classic cause of a slow LCP.

Checking PageSpeed one URL at a time gets old fast. This runs Lighthouse on a whole list of URLs, mobile or desktop, and returns scores, Core Web Vitals and the top fixes. No API key:
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/page-speed-core-web-vitals
Meeting recordings are searchable gold if they're text. Transcribe once, then you can search, quote and summarize instead of scrubbing through an hour of audio.
Render-blocking CSS and JS delay the first paint. Inline critical CSS, defer non-critical scripts, and load third-party widgets after the page is interactive.

Lab data vs field data: Lighthouse simulates a mid-range phone on a slow network. Real users may be faster or slower. Use lab tests to find problems, field data to confirm them.
Unused JavaScript is often the biggest Lighthouse opportunity. Check which scripts load on every page but are only needed on one, and split or lazy-load them.

Compare your homepage speed against competitors in one run: put all the URLs in, get performance scores and LCP/CLS side by side.
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/page-speed-core-web-vitals
Tip for podcasters: a transcript of each episode gives search engines text to index, helps deaf and hard-of-hearing listeners, and makes writing show notes much faster.
Layout shift (CLS) usually comes from images without width/height, ads or embeds that load late, and web fonts swapping. Reserve space for anything that loads after the text.
Japanese transcription tip: set the language to Japanese instead of auto-detect when the audio has a lot of English loanwords. It keeps the output in natural Japanese text.

Total Blocking Time is how long the main thread is too busy to respond. Heavy frameworks, chat widgets and tag managers are the usual suspects.

Interviews, lectures, voice memos: paste direct file links and get full text, timestamped segments and SRT subtitles back. Whisper, no API key needed:

Caching matters: static files like images, CSS and JS should have long cache lifetimes so repeat visitors don't download them again.
Before redesigning a slow site, measure it. Often three fixes (images, unused JS, a slow third-party script) recover most of the speed.

Year-end site check: one SEO + AI search readiness audit, one page speed run on your top pages. Fix the top 5 issues from each and you're ahead of most sites.
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/seo-ai-readiness-audit
Fonts can slow pages down too. Use font-display: swap, load only the weights you use, and consider system fonts for body text.
Whisper works best on clear audio. If you record meetings, a cheap external mic does more for transcript accuracy than any software setting.

Mobile scores are usually much lower than desktop in Lighthouse, and Google ranks on mobile. Test both in one run and see where the gap is:
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/page-speed-core-web-vitals
Accessibility and SEO overlap: alt text on images, descriptive link text, a clear heading structure and captions on videos help both humans and search engines.

Turn a backlog of recordings into text over the holidays: bulk transcription handles many files in one run, each with its own SRT file.
https://apify.com/mirumiru_miru17/audio-video-transcriber
Speed checklist: compressed images, lazy-loaded below-the-fold media, deferred JS, cached static files, few third-party scripts, a fast host. Six items, most of the gains.
Thanks for following this year. Plan for 2027: audit once a quarter, test speed after every release, and turn recordings into text instead of letting them pile up.
